title: The gold partition conjecture
formal: In every finite partial order that is not total, can one choose two consecutive comparisons so that t₀≥t₁+t₂ for every possible outcome path, where tᵢ counts the linear extensions remaining after i comparisons?
context:
Use the source's conventions for branches that finish sorting after the first comparison. The conjecture is stronger than the 1/3–2/3 question, which has its own significance.

This question was found through Wikipedia and compared individually with the existing candidate and archived records. The linked literature provides definitions and background; this import is not a completed research-card review.
why: A proposed stronger information guarantee for comparison sorting with partial-order information.
